extracted.intended_audience: PR practitioners, communications professionals, publicists, corporate comms teams pitching journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and practical guidance for assessing whether a story, press release, or pitch is 'newsworthy' and how to format an effective media pitch. Includes calendar triggers, elements of an effective story and pitch, implicit press-release-worthy claims, anti-patterns, and evolving content-marketing formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: A story that affects many people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the core PR newsworthiness tests — assess breadth of effect when deciding whether to pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant right now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use current events, recency, or news cycle alignment to make the story timely; avoid stale news (>48 hours).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: Involves notable people or organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories connected to well-known figures or brands increase pickup likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: Has local relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local angle matters for regional outlets; tailor pitches to geographic relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oddity
rubrics_metrics.description: An unusual or surprising angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unexpected or counterintuitive elements can generate interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product / service launch (calendar trigger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Product or service launch — focus on what's enabled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame launches around what customers can do now or new capabilities rather than self-congratulatory language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mergers & acquisitions (calendar trigger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcements about mergers and acquisitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain significance for market, customers, or industry to make it newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards & endorsements (calendar trigger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards and endorsements — especially industry-respected ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie awards to third-party validation and broader impact rather than internal praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: New executive hires (calendar trigger)
rubrics_metrics.description: New executive hires — especially senior appointments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the hire matters (strategy, experience, market signal) rather than just a personnel move.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expansion / new offices (calendar trigger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Company expansion or opening of new offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show local economic impact, jobs, or strategic reasons for expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layoffs / restructuring (calendar trigger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Layoffs or restructuring — handled proactively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use crisis-response best practices and proactive communication; sensitive timing and transparency are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anniversary milestones (calendar trigger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Company anniversaries (10th, 25th, 50th, 100th).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use milestone celebrations to reflect on impact, history, or future vision — tie to human stories or broader trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: New research / data (calendar trigger)
rubrics_metrics.description: New research or company-commissioned data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusive or proprietary data can provide journalists unique storylines — provide datasets, methodology, and expert interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership announcements (calendar trigger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcements of partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the partnership matters to customers, markets, or innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charity / philanthropy (calendar trigger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Charitable initiatives or philanthropic activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie to human stories, measurable impact, or community benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event sponsorship / hosting (calendar trigger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsoring or hosting events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize unique aspects, speakers, or outcomes; offer access to journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis response (calendar trigger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crisis response (limited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timely, factual responses; prioritize transparency and media-ready spokespeople.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trending topic commentary (calendar trigger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offering expert commentary on trending topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch experts aligned to the journalist's beat to provide timely color or analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey results (calendar trigger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Release of survey results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure methodological clarity, sample size, and relevance; exclusive or surprising findings increase interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine news value (story element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Story must have genuine news value rather than feeling like a press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pure promotional framing; emphasize new information, public relevance, or analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive data (story element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusive data journalists can't get elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide proprietary findings or unique datasets to differentiate the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert source (story element)
rubrics_metrics.description: An expert source who explains things clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer accessible spokespeople who can provide quotable insight and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely angle matching journalist's beat (story element)
rubrics_metrics.description: A timely angle that matches the journalist's beat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research reporters' coverage areas and tailor the angle to their interests and current stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling story arc (story element)
rubrics_metrics.description: A compelling narrative arc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame facts within human or trend-driven narratives to engage readers and reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual assets (story element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Photos, video, graphics to illustrate the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include ready-to-use visuals to increase pickup and storytelling options for journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line: clear, specific, news-y (pitch format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line should be clear, specific, and sound like news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft subject lines that convey the news hook in a concise phrase to increase open rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief body under 200 words (pitch format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the email body brief — under 200 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with the hook, follow with essential details, and keep length minimal for busy journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why this journalist specifically (pitch format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why you're pitching this particular journalist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personalize pitches by referencing past coverage or beat relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why this story now (pitch format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the timeliness/urgency — why the story matters now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly connect the pitch to current events, reporting cycles, or deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer interview / data / visuals (pitch format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer interviews, data access, or visual assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it easy for the reporter to pursue the story by offering materials and spokespeople.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo proposal if appropriate (pitch format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose an embargo when warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use embargoes to coordinate timed coverage, but be clear about terms and exclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: First / first-in-category (implicit press-release criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claiming to be the 'first' in some category (first-ever, first-to-market).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantiate first claims; being legitimately first is a strong news hook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biggest / largest (implicit press-release criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claiming to be the biggest or largest in some category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence for superlative claims; quantify scale and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-changing implication (implicit press-release criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that the development will change the industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support transformational claims with expert commentary, data, or demonstrable market effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterintuitive finding (implicit press-release criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings or angles that go against expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counterintuitive results can attract coverage — explain why they differ from assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-driven angle (implicit press-release criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: A data-driven or evidence-based angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists value rigorous data; be transparent about methods and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tied to news cycle (implicit press-release criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear tie-in to current news or events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link stories to ongoing coverage to increase relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tied to seasonal moment (implicit press-release criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tie to a seasonal moment or timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage seasonal beats (holidays, tax season, back-to-school) for relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tied to legislation / policy (implicit press-release criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: A connection to legislation or policy developments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain policy implications and provide expert analysis where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tied to celebrity / public figure (implicit press-release criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Association with celebrities or public figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Celebrity ties increase attention but must be relevant and substantive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holiday or anniversary peg (implicit press-release criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a holiday or anniversary as a peg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the peg meaningful rather than forced; connect to themes or human stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic announcement without angle (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic announcement lacking a clear angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pitching announcements without a news hook or context—journalists will ignore them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal achievement (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcements limited to internal organizational achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal-only relevance is not newsworthy for external media unless tied to broader impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-congratulatory press release (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-congratulatory or purely promotional press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame news in terms of public relevance, not corporate praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stale news (>48 hours) (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: News that is stale — older than ~48 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is critical; delay reduces media interest sharply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Untimely seasonal pitch (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Seasonal pitches that miss the appropriate timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan seasonal pitches in advance and align with editorial calendars.

rubrics_metrics.name: No data or evidence (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitches without supporting data or evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sources, figures, and methodology where claims rely on data.

rubrics_metrics.name: No human story (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of a human-interest element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human stories help make abstract topics relatable to readers and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: All-staff promotion of leadership (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mass promotion of leadership that reads like internal PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid blanket leadership promotion; frame leadership news around external impact or strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vague 'leading' or 'innovative' claims (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vague superlatives like 'leading' or 'innovative' without evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantiate claims with metrics, examples, or third-party validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-announcement of pre-announcement (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcing that you'll announce something later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid teaser announcements without tangible news; they rarely attract coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content-marketing formats filling news space (evolution/trend)
rubrics_metrics.description: PR-driven branded content, sponsored features, 'provided by' articles, and influencer-amplified pitches are increasingly occupying news space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize alternative routes to visibility (sponsored content, influencer amplification) while clearly labeling paid/partner content and balancing editorial credibility.
